title: Bitcoin Slides Toward $73,000 as Hot CPI Revives Fed Rate-Hike Bets
excerpt: October inflation rose 0.4 percent, above the 0.3 percent forecast, and core prices also beat expectations. Bitcoin fell to about $73,400 after the print, Treasury yields jumped, and traders now price a December Fed hike as near-certain, with a small chance of a half-point move.
body:
• US consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in October, above the 0.3 percent economists expected; core CPI rose 0.3 percent against a 0.2 percent forecast.
  • Bitcoin fell from about $74,300 before the release to roughly $73,400, and traded near $73,500 on Tuesday, down about 1 percent on the day.
  • Traders now price a Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting as near-certain: CME FedWatch put 85 percent odds on 25 basis points and 15 percent on 50 basis points, according to CoinDesk.
  • The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.99 percent, approaching 5 percent, tightening financial conditions across stocks, gold and crypto alike.

Bitcoin traded near $73,500 on Tuesday, down about 1 percent over the past day, after a hotter-than-expected US inflation report revived fears of a larger Federal Reserve rate hike, according to Bitcoin Magazine. The cryptocurrency had held near $74,300 in the minutes before the 8:30 a.m. ET release, dropped to about $73,400 right after the print, and steadied in the high $73,000s. CoinDesk put bitcoin at its weakest level since August 20, barely holding the $73,000 line.

The Inflation Print

The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the consumer price index rose 0.4 percent in October, down from 0.6 percent in September but above forecasts for 0.3 percent. Core CPI, which strips out food and energy, rose 0.3 percent against forecasts of 0.2 percent. No annual inflation rate was published with this report: the government shutdown in October 2025 prevented the BLS from collecting a full set of prices a year ago, so there is no comparable figure. Bank of America had estimated before the release that annual rates were running near 3.8 percent for headline and 2.7 percent for core.

How Markets Repriced

Bond traders moved first. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 13 basis points to 4.99 percent, and the two-year yield jumped to about 4.74 percent, according to CoinDesk. Nasdaq futures fell about 1.5 percent, and gold retreated alongside bitcoin. According to CME FedWatch figures cited by CoinDesk, traders put 85 percent odds on a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and 15 percent on a 50-basis-point move, with the odds of the Fed holding steady back at zero.

"In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting. Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take."

— Christopher Waller, Federal Reserve Governor, quoted by Bitcoin Magazine

Waller had laid out that scenario hours before the data landed, saying he was leaning toward a December increase and would back more robust action if inflation ran hotter than expected. Analysts cited by Bitcoin Magazine flagged $73,000 as the level to watch for bitcoin, with $70,000 the next downside marker if the selling extends.

What to Watch Next

Producer price data lands Friday, and minutes from the Fed's October meeting follow on November 18. The Fed's final meeting of the year is on December 8-9, and the next CPI report is due December 10. For crypto holders, the channel is straightforward: persistent inflation keeps yields near 5 percent, and yields at that level have repeatedly pulled money out of risk assets this year.
